title: Proportional Relationships
description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
objectives: Determine if a relationship is proportional

lessons.title: Proportional vs Non-Proportional
lessons.content: A proportional relationship has a constant ratio (unit rate) and passes through the origin.
examples: y = 3x + 2 is NOT proportional (doesn't pass through origin)

lessons.title: Equations and Graphs
lessons.content: Write y = kx where k is the constant of proportionality.
examples: If a car travels 55 mph: d = 55t
Graph is a straight line through (0,0)

title: Rational Number Operations
description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers including fractions and negatives.
objectives: Apply rules for operations with rational numbers
Solve multi-step problems with rational numbers
Convert between fractions, decimals, and percents

lessons.title: Operations with Rational Numbers
lessons.content: Combine integer rules with fraction rules.

lessons.title: Multi-Step Problems
lessons.content: Apply multiple operations in the correct order.
examples: A temperature drops 3/2 degrees per hour for 4 hours: −3/2 × 4 = −6°

title: Expressions and the Distributive Property
description: Expand and factor expressions using the distributive property.

lessons.title: Factoring
lessons.content: Reverse the distributive property by pulling out the GCF.

title: Equations and Inequalities — Multi-Step
description: Solve multi-step equations and inequalities with rational numbers.
objectives: Write equations and inequalities for word problems

lessons.title: Multi-Step Equations
lessons.content: Use inverse operations and the distributive property to solve.

lessons.title: Inequalities
lessons.content: Solving is like equations, but flip the inequality sign when multiplying/dividing by negatives.

title: Geometry — Scale Drawings
description: Use scale factors to create and interpret scale drawings and models.
objectives: Find actual dimensions from scale drawings

lessons.title: Scale Factor
lessons.content: A scale factor is the ratio of a drawing length to actual length.
examples: Scale 1:100 means 1 cm on drawing = 100 cm in reality
A room 4 cm on map with scale 1:50 is 200 cm = 2 m real
Floor plan: bedroom 6 cm × 4 cm at 1:24 scale → 144 cm × 96 cm real

title: Geometry — Circles
description: Understand the parts of a circle; calculate circumference and area.

lessons.title: Circumference
lessons.content: The perimeter of a circle is called circumference: C = πd = 2πr.

title: Statistics — Comparing Populations
description: Use measures of center and variability to compare two data sets.
objectives: Calculate and compare medians and means
Compare variability using IQR and MAD

lessons.title: Comparing Data Sets
lessons.content: Use box plots and statistics to compare two populations.
examples: Class A median = 78, IQR = 12; Class B median = 72, IQR = 20 → A has higher center and less spread
Use double box plots for visual comparison

lessons.title: Sampling
lessons.content: A random sample is used to make inferences about a population.
examples: Survey 30 randomly selected students to estimate school opinion
Larger samples give more reliable estimates

title: Probability — Compound Events
description: Calculate probabilities of compound events using lists, trees, and tables.
objectives: List all outcomes in a sample space

lessons.title: Sample Space
lessons.content: All possible outcomes can be organized in a table or tree diagram.
examples: Flipping 2 coins: HH, HT, TH, TT → 4 outcomes
Rolling a die and flipping a coin: 6 × 2 = 12 outcomes

lessons.title: Independent Events
lessons.content: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) for independent events.

title: Percent Applications
description: Apply percent to tax, tip, discount, markup, and interest.

lessons.title: Tax, Tip, and Discount
lessons.content: Multiply the percent (as decimal) by the original price.

lessons.title: Simple Interest
lessons.content: I = Prt where P = principal, r = rate, t = time in years.

title: Geometry — 3D Figures
description: Find surface area and volume of prisms, pyramids, and cylinders.
objectives: Calculate surface area of prisms and pyramids
Calculate volume of prisms and cylinders

lessons.title: Surface Area
lessons.content: Sum of the areas of all faces.
examples: Square pyramid: 1 square base + 4 triangular faces

lessons.title: Volume of Cylinders
examples: Soup can r = 4 cm, h = 12 cm: V ≈ 603.2 cm³
